B3.title: RUN/STOP break x DMA transport in flight

transport_state_machine.safe_exit: the job has not been submitted; the caller may return to the evaluator boundary

transport_state_machine.break_action: latch only while DMA/convergence state remains owned by the seam

transport_state_machine.poll_or_longjmp: still forbidden until the seam has restored its descriptor, scratch and map invariants
transport_state_machine.safe_exit: return status to the first outer evaluator boundary

transport_state_machine.break_action: consume the one pending latch and enter the sole C2J-aware abort landing

invariants: No product DMA submit, convergence or content-proof closure calls lisp_poll, lisp_abort, longjmp or the C2J abort landing.
A RUN/STOP edge may set one pending bit during any transport state but may not unwind that state.
The pending bit is idempotent: repeated samples of one held press do not create multiple aborts.
The first safe evaluator boundary consumes the pending bit exactly once before the next Lisp evaluator step.
Descriptor bytes, transport scratch, C2D, C2J, exports and both Chip planes equal the corresponding no-break outcome until the normal abort landing performs its contracted rollback.

required_observations: no non-local exit before the safe boundary

B3.closure: reviewed addendum plus linked closure inventory and all cutpoints green for every product DMA seam

C3.title: Freezer x handoff state machine

platform_distinction.freezer: double-RESTORE enters hypervisor trap 0x42 at an instruction-fetch boundary; it is not the guest NMI vector
platform_distinction.guest_nmi: guest NMI remains independently possible and is not masked by SEI
platform_distinction.rule: Freezer and guest NMI are separate proof obligations; neither may be inferred safe from IRQ masking

source_less_irq_episode.state: C2K_SOURCELESS_IRQS at $FF86 is an episode latch, not a session counter
source_less_irq_episode.reset: every owned raster IRQ clears the latch before frame progress is published
source_less_irq_episode.allow: the first source-less return IRQ after an owned raster IRQ is accepted and sets the latch
source_less_irq_episode.reject: a second consecutive source-less IRQ without an intervening owned raster IRQ fails closed
source_less_irq_episode.freezer_sequence: source-less, owned-raster, source-less is legal for arbitrarily many Freezer episodes
source_less_irq_episode.storm_sequence: source-less, source-less without owned-raster progress remains fail-closed

cutpoints.only_legal_continuation: resume the exact frozen firmware-owned instruction; later C2 ownership begins from its first check

cutpoints.interval: replacement-armed after SEI and before MAP commit
cutpoints.only_legal_continuation: resume the exact handoff instruction; no product vector, evaluator or session path is reachable; the remaining handoff checks run fresh

cutpoints.interval: handoff-closed after MAP commit and before product-owned publication
cutpoints.only_legal_continuation: resume only inside the handoff closure and complete map, vector, abort and frame validation before product-owned publication; any owner/identity mismatch fails closed
the identity-specific Freezer return proof validates map generation, vectors, E000 and both Chip planes before the fixture permits ordinary evaluator work

nmi_rules: The closure active at a cutpoint may return only to the same cutpoint interval; it may not jump directly to an evaluator or publish a later state.
The C2 NMI handler acknowledges only its owned source, preserves the complete machine context, allocates nothing and calls no Lisp.
An NMI observed while C2K_STATE is not product-owned cannot manufacture product-owned state.
A vector may become authoritative only after its complete target bytes and mapping are authoritative.

host_state_machine: Freezer trap and guest NMI classified separately
two Freezer returns separated by owned raster progress are accepted
two consecutive source-less IRQs without raster progress fail closed

hardware.method: a non-promotable cutpoint carrier resumes into a verifier, never directly into Lisp; the verifier either records the exact owner tuple and stops or fails closed
hardware.determinism_rule: a cutpoint not deterministically reachable on the pinned core is not silently skipped; it remains OPEN with the precise platform limitation

C3.closure: reviewed addendum, complete host cutpoint matrix and all deterministically reachable hardware cutpoints green; no speculative resume

D3.title: typed queue overflow x break delivery

pinned_source.meaning: physical RUN/STOP level independent of the typed event queue

queue_fact.overflow_behavior: a sixth event is not enqueued while the five-event queue is full

source_rule: RUN/STOP abort identity comes only from the matrix edge source, never from PETSCII table interpretation.
The selector is fixed before the owned raster IRQ is enabled; the IRQ samples D613 bit 7.
Released arms the source. The first active-low sample while armed sets pending and disarms. Held samples do nothing. A released sample rearms.
A typed queue head with PETSCII 0x03 is captured and dequeued exactly once but is discarded as an abort source, preventing duplicate delivery of the same physical press.
All non-RUN/STOP queue tuples retain their original code/modifier order and exactly-once dequeue semantics.
The pending matrix break is out-of-band from ordinary tuple order and is consumed exactly once at the B3 safe evaluator boundary.
D3.single_truth_rule: segment 7, bit 7 and PETSCII 0x03 are generated by a source-identity gate from the pinned core matrix ordinal 63; no product-local keymap table is permitted

hardware_sequence: hold product consumption and fill the typed queue with five distinct ordinary code/modifier tuples
prove the head plus four buffered events from the pinned core model
press and release physical RUN/STOP while the queue remains full
observe exactly one abort at the first safe evaluator boundary
drain and compare all five ordinary tuples in original order
prove a later queued PETSCII 0x03 cannot cause a second abort
negative_cases: matrix press not latched while queue full

D3.closure: source-identity gate and queue-full physical hardware fixture green with exactly one abort and five unchanged ordinary tuples

E5.title: bounded nesting four x user-visible error

detail.meaning: the refused transient depth; the configured maximum remains four

error.registry_rule: append after current code 62 and raise LISP65_ERROR_CODE_LIMIT from 63 to 64; all prior numeric identities remain byte-for-byte unchanged

failure_order: read and authenticate the current transient depth
if the requested depth is five, set the stable innermost status and Fixnum detail
return before C2J publication, Attic write, record write, watermark change, export write or READY change
render through the normal L65E/Lisp error surface
state_postcondition: C2D header and all active rows byte-identical

fixture.surface: real eval calling nested eval until the fifth transient installation is requested
required_cases: depths one through four execute and restore exact state
depth five renders LISP65_ERR_C2_NESTING_DEPTH with Fixnum 5
depth five is catchable by the normal Lisp error boundary
the exact pre-call state is restored
a subsequent ordinary expression returns t

E5.closure: append-only registry and renderer gates green plus depth-five end-to-end fixture with exact state and usable REPL
